edit.description: globToRegex: compile `**`/`*` without substituting a placeholder literal
extend the literal-path pin past single characters to multi-character sentinel text

summary: globToRegex round-trips `**` through a `::DOUBLESTAR::` literal, so a glob carrying that text compiles to `.*` and admits every path

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

acceptance: matchesAny admits only the declared path for a glob containing the compiler's placeholder text; the write guard, the queue fence and ship detection see no wildcard the glob never spelled.
tests: a declared path containing the glob compiler's `**` placeholder text matches only itself
notes: Verified on disk: matchesAny('src/secret.ts', ['::DOUBLESTAR::']) -> true; matchesAny('docs/anything-else.md', ['docs/::DOUBLESTAR::.md']) -> true (src/paths.ts:124-127). Same class as the fixed `?` hole, which was pitched at the hand-kept escape class — a per-character pin cannot see a multi-character hole. Splitting on `**` then `*` removes the placeholder rather than escaping around it.
